text:
Sam Malinski was one of the best defensemen in the league last season by Evolving-Hockey's numbers, eighth of 215 in wins above replacement, and most people outside Denver couldn't pick him out of a lineup. He's undrafted, out of Cornell, and now playing almost 18 minutes a night for Colorado.

This season he has seven assists and no goals in 17 games, with six points in his last ten. His ice time is up more than a minute and a half over that stretch. The Avalanche have 51% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, a little worse than without him, and they've scored 7.7 more goals than expected when he's out there, which has padded his assists.

The bigger case for him is last season: Evolving-Hockey had him driving play (96th percentile) and taking chances away (99th), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.8 primary shot assists per 60 (95th percentile among defensemen). Our projection: about 37 points.
